_comment: Pairformer trunk (AlphaFold3), contact prediction. Identical to 02_evoformer/ds_config.json on purpose -- the architectures are being compared, so everything except the architecture is held fixed. Read the ZeRO note below before changing the stage -- this is the one example in the course where the ZeRO stage is nearly irrelevant, and understanding why is the point of the topic.
_batch_comment: train_batch_size is DELIBERATELY OMITTED so DeepSpeed derives it as micro x accum x num_gpus and any --num_gpus works without editing this file. The unit here is a CHAIN (one protein with its MSA), not a token: micro=2 means two proteins per rank per step. Two is small on purpose -- the activation cost scales with N_res^3, so batch size is the cheapest knob to turn when a longer protein will not fit.
_precision_comment: bf16 on, and this one is NOT optional. DS4Sci_EvoformerAttention accepts fp16 and bf16 only -- it has no fp32 path -- so --ds-evoformer-attn requires one of them to be enabled here. bf16 over fp16 because the triangle attention logits are a sum over a third residue index and fp16's narrow range is exactly where that overflows. bf16 needs Ampere (A100 / RTX 3090) or newer; on Volta or Turing switch to fp16, but never enable both or DeepSpeed raises at initialization.
_zero_comment: Stage 1, and the reason is the whole topic. ZeRO shards optimizer state (stage 1), gradients (stage 2) and parameters (stage 3). This model has ~100k parameters. Sharding it harder would trade communication for kilobytes while the thing actually filling the card -- an O(N_res^3) triangle attention logit tensor -- is an ACTIVATION, which no ZeRO stage touches. Every rank materialises it in full, every step. That is why the answer here is a fused kernel (--ds-evoformer-attn) and activation checkpointing, not a higher stage. Raising the stage to fit a longer protein is the single most tempting wrong move in this lab. MEASURED on 1x RTX 3080 Ti at --n-res 128: stage 1 = 0.65 GB, stage 3 = 0.62 GB. A 4.6% difference, for 1.5x the communication.
_bucket_comment: reduce_bucket_size is set EXPLICITLY, and that matters more than it looks. Leave it out and DeepSpeed defaults it to 5e8 -- a 500 MB reduction buffer -- while ds_config_z3.json sets 16 MB. The first version of these two files differed in exactly that way, so the ZeRO-1-vs-ZeRO-3 comparison this lab invites read 1.58 GB vs 0.62 GB and appeared to show stage 3 winning by 2.5x. It was measuring the buckets, not the stage. These two configs are now identical except for the stage, which is the only way the comparison means anything.
_checkpointing_comment: Activation checkpointing is configured but left OFF by default so the baseline measurement is honest. Turn it on with --activation-checkpointing to recompute the triangle activations in the backward pass instead of storing them: real memory relief, at roughly 30% more compute. Unlike the ZeRO stage, this one attacks the tensor that is actually large.
